title: Media literacy
learning_outcomes: Explain reporting versus commentary in the context of media literacy.
Compare and distinguish source verification in the context of media literacy.
Apply framing and manipulation in the context of media literacy.
Evaluate and justify decisions about fact-checking in the context of media literacy.

lessons.title: Reporting versus commentary
lessons.outcome: Explain reporting versus commentary in the context of media literacy.
lessons.worked_example_brief: Use a realistic fictional case involving reporting versus commentary; show reasoning, a contrasting case and limitations.
lessons.practice: Create an annotated explanation with a concrete example and a counterexample. Connect the result to verification dossier.
lessons.knowledge_check: Explain reporting versus commentary from memory and apply it to a different example; state one limitation.
lessons.evidence_criterion: Accurate explanation of reporting versus commentary; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.

lessons.title: Source verification
lessons.outcome: Compare and distinguish source verification in the context of media literacy.
lessons.worked_example_brief: Use a realistic fictional case involving source verification; show reasoning, a contrasting case and limitations.
lessons.practice: Compare two cases or approaches using explicit criteria; identify an important limitation. Connect the result to verification dossier.
lessons.knowledge_check: Explain source verification from memory and apply it to a different example; state one limitation.
lessons.evidence_criterion: Accurate explanation of source verification; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.

lessons.title: Framing and manipulation
lessons.outcome: Apply framing and manipulation in the context of media literacy.
lessons.worked_example_brief: Use a realistic fictional case involving framing and manipulation; show reasoning, a contrasting case and limitations.
lessons.practice: Work through a new case or simulation; document assumptions and steps. Connect the result to verification dossier.
lessons.knowledge_check: Explain framing and manipulation from memory and apply it to a different example; state one limitation.
lessons.evidence_criterion: Accurate explanation of framing and manipulation; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.

lessons.title: Fact-checking
lessons.outcome: Evaluate and justify decisions about fact-checking in the context of media literacy.
lessons.worked_example_brief: Use a realistic fictional case involving fact-checking; show reasoning, a contrasting case and limitations.
lessons.practice: Analyse an unfamiliar case; defend a choice, identify uncertainty and revise after feedback. Connect the result to verification dossier.
lessons.knowledge_check: Explain fact-checking from memory and apply it to a different example; state one limitation.
lessons.evidence_criterion: Accurate explanation of fact-checking; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.

criteria.criterion: Accurate explanation of reporting versus commentary; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.
Accurate explanation of source verification; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.
Accurate explanation of framing and manipulation; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.
Accurate explanation of fact-checking; correct application to a new case; clear rationale and limits.

assessment.threshold: All mapped criteria at level 2; no averaging away missing criteria. Level 3 requires independent novel application, delayed reassessment and appropriate review.
assessment.alternate_evidence: Equivalent accessible written, oral, visual, simulated or supervised evidence; no personal disclosure required.
assessment.reviewer: Historian, economist, legal or policy specialist as appropriate.

safety.notes: Respect consent, privacy and applicable rules; source and subject review before publication.
